limitations: A curated source snapshot, not a complete import graph, runtime trace, or execution order.
All registered context topics and top-level production packages have an entry point. Internal classes, algorithms, runtime paths, and relationships remain selectively represented.
References through protocols and injected factories are scoped to the described production assembly.
Source-reviewed means checked against the pinned source revision; it is not a physical qualification result.
Static extraction scans the selected node source files only. Topic or package representation is not a completeness claim.

nodes.label: TaskProgramCfg
nodes.summary: Declarative task configuration describing intent and execution structure.
boundaries: Configuration alone does not execute a simulation.
nodes.details: Start here when describing an embodied task declaratively. The configuration records the program structure and targets that the compiler validates before execution; the same language can be supplied through JSON, YAML, or Python.

nodes.label: TaskProgramCompiler
nodes.summary: Compiles task configuration into an analysable program using a static scene manifest.
boundaries: Program compilation and runtime semantic lowering are separate stages.
nodes.details: This is the static compilation stage. It validates a task against scene contracts and materializes bounded program segments. Runtime lowering remains a separate concern, so inspecting a compiled program does not require executing its robot actions.

nodes.label: CompiledTaskProgram
nodes.summary: Immutable compilation result with materialized task segments and analysis views.
boundaries: The result is not a control command or proof of successful physical execution.
nodes.details: The compiler expands the task into immutable, already materialized segments. Consumers can iterate those segments and inspect analyses before handing them to an execution integration. The object describes intended work, not its physical outcome.

nodes.label: TaskProgramEnvironmentAdapter
nodes.summary: Validates integration choices and assembles the semantic runtime and Gym bridge.
boundaries: Live data and concrete services are supplied by the environment factory.
nodes.details: This adapter connects the task language to a concrete environment. It validates the chosen integration and assembles the semantic executor, command buffer, shared clock, and demonstration bridge used by the Gym workflow.

nodes.label: SimulationTaskProgramFactory
nodes.summary: Binds simulated robots, planners, and services to construct the atomic skill engine.
boundaries: This simulation factory does not own runtime-independent program compilation.
nodes.details: The simulation factory supplies the concrete robot and planning services required by a Task Program integration. It resolves planner configuration, creates the motion generator, and constructs an atomic engine with the selected control profile.

nodes.label: SemanticCallCompiler
nodes.summary: Analyses and lowers Semantic Calls against the bound scene and skill integration.
boundaries: Runtime semantic lowering is separate from static TaskProgramCompiler compilation.
nodes.details: Semantic Calls express high-level task intent. This compiler analyzes and lowers those calls against the bound scene and skill integration, keeping semantic interpretation separate from transport and environment stepping.

nodes.label: SemanticCallExecutor
nodes.summary: Lowers and executes semantic calls, creating an execution session for each call.
boundaries: Execution sessions do not span call boundaries.
nodes.details: At runtime, the executor lowers a call and starts an atomic execution session for its grounded invocation. It connects that session to observations, the selected command sink, and the execution clock through an ExecutionRunner.

nodes.label: AtomicActionEngine
nodes.summary: Manages planning resources and atomic skills to create executable action sessions.
boundaries: Commands are dispatched by ExecutionRunner and its command sink.
nodes.details: Atomic Skills form the typed boundary between semantic intent and executable action plans. The engine owns planning resources and creates execution sessions. A runner and command sink dispatch commands; the engine itself does not advance the environment.

nodes.label: MotionGenerator
nodes.summary: Composes planning backends behind a unified robot motion generation interface.
boundaries: This entry point belongs to motion and is not re-exported by planners.
nodes.details: Use this entry point to turn joint or end-effector goals into timed trajectories. It composes planner backends behind one motion interface, while simulation playback or Atomic Skills consume the generated motion.

nodes.label: ExecutionRunner
nodes.summary: Advances atomic skill sessions through observation, command, and clock interfaces.
boundaries: Command acceptance does not imply a completed physical state transition.
nodes.details: The runner advances an atomic session through observation, command, and clock interfaces. Its command sink determines where commands go. Acknowledgement of a command is distinct from confirmation that a physical effect has occurred.

nodes.label: TaskProgramDemoBridge
nodes.summary: Converts program segments into lazy Gym demonstrations with a shared runtime, buffer, and clock.
boundaries: This view focuses on sequential execution, not all parallel scheduling or recovery paths.
nodes.details: The bridge exposes program execution as incremental Gym demonstrations. It shares a buffered command sink and environment-step clock with the semantic runtime, so action consumption and time progression stay coordinated with the host environment.

nodes.label: BufferedGymCommandSink
nodes.summary: Validates and buffers control commands for incremental Gym demonstration consumption.
boundaries: Accepting a buffered command does not mean the environment has stepped.
nodes.details: This sink validates and encodes runtime commands, then buffers controller actions for the Gym demonstration generator. It is the handoff between command dispatch and later environment consumption, rather than a direct call to simulation stepping.

nodes.label: EnvironmentStepClock
nodes.summary: Maintains execution time on the environment step grid.
boundaries: Time advances through the Gym bridge handshake; sleeping does not advance simulation.
nodes.details: Execution time is tied to the environment step grid. The Gym bridge and command sink use the same clock instance, allowing timing checks to stay aligned with the environment handshake instead of wall-clock sleeps.

nodes.label: EmbodiedEnv
nodes.summary: Assembles scenes, managers, and demonstrations with optional Task Program integration.
boundaries: Language definitions, compilation, and semantic runtime belong to task_program.
nodes.details: Use this configuration-driven environment to assemble a robot task from scene objects, sensors, and manager-owned behavior. It extends the shared Gym lifecycle and optionally connects Task Program compilation and demonstrations through an environment adapter.

nodes.label: BaseEnv
nodes.summary: Owns the Gym loop, simulation initialisation, and environment step lifecycle.
boundaries: Simulation state advances through the environment lifecycle.
nodes.details: This is the common Gymnasium-compatible lifecycle beneath embodied tasks. It initializes the simulation manager and coordinates reset, stepping, and environment timing. Higher-level environments add task-specific scene assembly and behavior.

nodes.label: SimulationManager
nodes.summary: Manages the world, robots, sensors, physics, and visualisation lifecycle.
boundaries: This explorer displays source relationships without starting the simulation runtime.
nodes.details: The simulation manager is the central owner of the simulated world. It creates and retains scene entities, coordinates physics and sensors, and starts optional browser visualization. Environment and task layers access the world through this API.

nodes.label: CLI
nodes.summary: Dispatches commands and lazily loads task discovery, environment, and training entry points.
boundaries: Task and runtime behaviour remain with their respective modules.
nodes.details: The unified embodichain command resolves a requested subcommand and loads its handler lazily. Use the CLI reference to find launch options for environments, training, assets, and other tools; task behavior stays in the handler-owned subsystem.

nodes.label: Official tasks
nodes.summary: Registers official task entry points and organises reusable robot tasks.
boundaries: Task configurations and Python registration entry points have separate owners.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Official task environments for EmbodiChain.

Importing this package triggers auto-registration of all task environments
via recursive module import. Each task-named module executes its
``@register_env`` decorator, registering the environment in gymnasium's global
registry.
"""

nodes.details: Official tasks are bundled in the same distribution under the embodichain_tasks import package. Import-backed tasks register during discovery, while supported configuration-defined Task Programs register when their Gym configuration is loaded.

nodes.label: Component composition
nodes.summary: Resolves environment and embodiment components into runnable Gym configurations.
boundaries: Deployment configurations cannot duplicate fields owned by selected components.

evidence.excerpt: """Resolve reusable environment and embodiment Gym components."""

nodes.details: Reusable environment and embodiment components separate physical scene ownership from robot, sensor, and Task Program selections. Composition resolves those selections into the deployment configuration and rejects duplicated component-owned fields.

nodes.label: Managers
nodes.summary: Organises observations, actions, rewards, events, and data recording within the environment lifecycle.
boundaries: Each manager defines the calling signature of its functors.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Managers that orchestrate collections of functors (observation, reward, event, action, dataset) running at specific points in the environment step loop.

Each manager owns a typed ``@configclass`` config whose attributes are ``FunctorCfg`` instances; the config attribute name becomes the functor's unique identifier.
"""

nodes.details: Managers organize task behavior around observations, actions, rewards, events, and dataset recording. Each manager invokes functors with its own contract, letting tasks compose behavior while sharing the environment reset and step lifecycle.

nodes.label: Planners
nodes.summary: Provides motion planning backends that generate constrained robot trajectories.
boundaries: The MotionGenerator composition entry point belongs to the motion module.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Motion planning stack.

``BasePlanner`` trajectory planners (TOPPRA, trapezoidal, neural, and cuRobo)
produce joint trajectories from waypoints. Motion generation composes these
backends in ``embodichain.lab.sim.motion.motion_generator``.
"""

nodes.details: Planning backends produce robot trajectories with different timing, geometric, or collision constraints. Choose a backend through motion configuration; use MotionGenerator as the composition entry point when building a complete motion request.

nodes.label: Solvers
nodes.summary: Provides inverse kinematics backends and stateful robot solving capabilities.
boundaries: Shared numerical algorithms belong to compute; stateful solvers remain in sim.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Inverse-kinematics solvers sharing the ``BaseSolver`` interface.

Provides analytic (SRS, OPW, UR, FEP), numerical (Pinocchio, Pink, Differential), and learning-based (PyTorch, NeuralIK) solvers, one per robot control part.
"""

nodes.details: Kinematic solvers map joint positions to poses and find joint positions for target poses. This layer contains robot-aware solver state and backend selection. Shared numerical routines belong to compute, while timed trajectories belong to motion planning.

nodes.label: Robot
nodes.summary: Represents a simulated robot with control parts, joint state, and kinematics.
boundaries: Robot presets and live entity state are managed separately.
nodes.details: The robot facade exposes simulated joint state, control parts, and kinematic capabilities. SimulationManager creates and retains the live entity; robot presets and configuration describe how it should be assembled.

nodes.label: Sensors
nodes.summary: Provides camera, stereo, and contact observations for the environment.
boundaries: Contact-data adaptation belongs to sensors; shared computation belongs to compute.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Sensors attached to the simulation scene.

``Camera``, ``StereoCamera``, and ``ContactSensor`` all derive from ``BaseSensor`` and expose batched ``TensorDict`` data buffers.
"""

nodes.details: Sensors turn simulation state into batched observations. Camera, stereo, and contact sensors expose different data contracts and configuration choices. Sensor-specific adaptation stays here, while reusable numerical image and geometry routines belong to compute.

nodes.label: Physics backends
nodes.summary: Constructs the configured physics backend and connects simulation state to physics solving.
boundaries: Environment files declare default or newton; launch arguments do not switch backends.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Physics backend registry and factory.

Selects a concrete :class:`PhysicsBackend` from a physics config via
:func:`embodichain.lab.sim.cfg.physics_backend_from_cfg` and instantiates it
with the owning :class:`SimulationManager` as its back-reference.
"""

nodes.details: The physics layer constructs the backend selected by the environment file and connects scene state to physics solving. Default and Newton configurations have separate owners; a launcher can confirm the file selection but does not switch its backend.

nodes.label: Browser visualization
nodes.summary: Publishes simulation snapshots and interactive controls through a browser runtime.
boundaries: Simulation reads run on the simulation thread; backend updates run on the visualisation worker.
nodes.details: The browser runtime publishes simulation snapshots and interactive controls. Simulation reads remain on the simulation thread, while the visualization worker handles backend updates. This module visualizes a running world; this architecture explorer visualizes code structure.

nodes.label: Compute
nodes.summary: Shared numerical algorithms for kinematics, trajectories, geometry, and images.
boundaries: Does not depend on lab, simulation objects, or environment managers.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Array and tensor computations shared across simulation, planning, and tools.

Domain packages own their algorithms; private ``_warp`` packages contain Warp
implementations. Importing this package does not initialize a simulator or
load any computation backend."""

nodes.details: Compute provides reusable numerical routines for kinematics, trajectories, geometry, and images. Its dependency boundary excludes lab objects and environment managers, allowing higher-level robotics modules to share algorithms without owning their runtime lifecycle.

nodes.label: Standard trainer
nodes.summary: Coordinates standard rollout collection, algorithm updates, evaluation, and checkpoints.
boundaries: Standard rollout storage is separate from the graph-connected differentiable training route.
nodes.details: The standard Trainer creates a SyncCollector and RolloutBuffer, retains the selected policy and algorithm, and schedules collection and updates. Simulator Gym deployments and standard lightweight environments use this path. Differentiable algorithms select a separate trainer.

nodes.label: OnlineDataEngine
nodes.summary: Online data engine managing workers and their lifecycle.
boundaries: The data pipeline owns worker persistence and error propagation.
nodes.details: The online data workflow connects simulation producers with training consumers. An OnlineDataEngine manages shared trajectory data, while OnlineDataset exposes sampling through PyTorch dataset patterns. See the streaming guide for lifecycle, buffering, and sampling behavior.

nodes.label: Scene generation
nodes.summary: Generates scene state from input images for scene asset workflows.
boundaries: Scene generation and simulation execution have independent lifecycles.
nodes.details: The Scene Engine turns image inputs into scene-state and asset workflows for simulation preparation. Scene generation has its own pipeline lifecycle; loading and executing the resulting scene in a simulation is a separate responsibility.

nodes.label: Devices
nodes.summary: Defines start, stop, and controller-state interfaces for robot input devices.
boundaries: The interface alone does not provide a hardware driver or execute robot actions.

evidence.excerpt: import abc  # for abstract base class definitions

nodes.details: Device is an abstract controller-state interface. DeviceController consumes implementations to map input to robot actions. Concrete device I/O and the host action-application loop are separate responsibilities.

nodes.label: Environment launcher
nodes.summary: Runs task discovery, configuration loading, and Gym environment creation.
boundaries: Environment creation is dispatched through the registered Gym ID; task-specific behaviour stays with the environment.

evidence.excerpt: def cli(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None:

nodes.details: The run-env launcher discovers task packages, decodes the selected deployment, and creates the registered Gym environment. Use its launch guide to inspect a task, configure a run, and understand where configuration becomes a live environment.

nodes.label: Config loader
nodes.summary: Loads deployment files, resolves components, and assembles the typed environment configuration.
boundaries: Configuration assembly precedes runtime creation. This module does not itself step the environment.
nodes.details: The loader decodes deployment files, resolves reusable components, and assembles typed environment configuration. It connects command-line inputs to environment construction, while leaving simulation stepping to the environment lifecycle.

nodes.label: Task discovery
nodes.summary: Imports installed task packages through entry points to populate the environment registry.
boundaries: Discovery is dynamic and depends on installed task packages; this view only links the official package.
nodes.details: Task discovery loads installed packages declared through the embodichain.tasks entry-point group. These imports populate the environment registry. The official task package is one selected example; actual discovery depends on the installed packages.

nodes.label: Data assets
nodes.summary: Resolves asset paths and coordinates registered dataset downloads and caches.
nodes.details: Asset lookup can resolve a local path or instantiate a registered dataset to download and extract its assets. This layer owns asset discovery and cache roots; online trajectory sampling and demonstration recording are separate workflows.
boundaries: Asset lookup may trigger downloads; it does not generate or record demonstrations.

nodes.label: MLLM frontend
nodes.summary: Decodes untrusted model JSON and compiles it through the existing Task Program adapter.
nodes.details: The host supplies trusted integration settings. The frontend admits a restricted sequential subset, validates model-provided content, and delegates compilation to the canonical environment adapter. It does not introduce a separate model-specific compiler.
boundaries: This is an input boundary, not an autonomous model service or a robot execution loop.

evidence.excerpt: """Strict MLLM frontend for declarative Task Program JSON responses."""

nodes.label: Toolkit directory
nodes.summary: Standalone grasp sampling, collision-mesh preparation, and URDF assembly utilities.
nodes.details: Three standalone asset-preparation branches: GraspKit, URDF Assembly, and Convex Decomposition. Choose a branch for its input/output contract and public entry point. This package directory does not execute the tools as one pipeline.
boundaries: Toolkit operations do not own the simulation lifecycle.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Standalone asset-preparation and manipulation utilities usable independently of the simulation loop.

Includes parallel-gripper grasp sampling, URDF convex decomposition, and URDF assembly.
"""

nodes.label: Configuration utilities
nodes.summary: Defines typed configuration copying, serialization, and required-field validation.
nodes.details: The configclass decorator wraps dataclasses and provides independent defaults, copying, updates, and validation. Domain loaders still own schema and value constraints. Configuration construction may leave required values unresolved until validate is called.
boundaries: Required-field validation is not universal type or domain validation.

nodes.label: Robot workspace
nodes.summary: Loads reachability caches and samples robot joint configurations and poses.
nodes.details: Robot-facing workspace sampling reuses offline analysis results and recomputes poses with the current robot base. Cached samples include validity masks and optional metrics. Offline analysis and runtime cache consumption have separate lifecycles.
boundaries: Kinematic reachability does not establish collision freedom or task success.

nodes.label: Workspace analyzer
nodes.summary: Analyzes robot reachability and metrics for reusable workspace caches.
nodes.details: The analyzer combines sampling, FK or IK, constraints, metrics, and result caching. Select an analysis mode and robot control part explicitly, then consume compatible caches through the runtime workspace interface.
boundaries: Offline analysis is distinct from runtime motion planning.

nodes.label: Trajectory augmentation
nodes.summary: Tracks trajectory candidates, generation budgets, coverage, and commit receipts.
nodes.details: The expansion package provides candidate contracts, residual and retiming operators, coverage metrics, and bounded session bookkeeping. Host integrations supply rollout execution, initial-state restoration, physical validation, and durable recording.
boundaries: GenerationSession does not step or reset environments and does not write datasets.

nodes.label: DifferentiableEnv
nodes.summary: Preserves the Gym lifecycle while bridging task-defined kinematics to autograd.
nodes.details: A Newton-backed environment records a task-defined kinematic callback on a Warp tape and exposes gradients through PyTorch. It requires gradient-enabled Newton configuration and coordinates terminal resets with backward completion.
boundaries: This environment does not run the Newton dynamics solver; it is not the lightweight APG trainer route.

nodes.label: Newton autograd bridge
nodes.summary: Connects Warp tape derivatives to PyTorch action and functional-state gradients.
nodes.details: The bridge executes a supplied kinematic callback and exposes selected outputs to autograd. Task hooks own action mapping and output contracts; the bridge carries gradient information across the Warp and PyTorch boundary.
boundaries: A differentiable kinematic step is not a differentiable dynamics simulation.

nodes.label: Domain randomization
nodes.summary: Event functors randomize physical, visual, spatial, and geometric properties.
nodes.details: Configure randomizers as EventCfg entries. EventManager dispatches them at startup, reset, or interval boundaries with the configured seed policy. Randomizers share the event mechanism while keeping property-specific behavior in their own modules.
boundaries: Randomization scheduling belongs to EventManager.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Domain-randomization event functors (physics, visual, spatial, geometry).

Implemented as event functors registered via ``EventCfg`` and dispatched by ``EventManager`` at startup / reset / interval modes.
"""

nodes.label: EventManager
nodes.summary: Dispatches configured event functors with lifecycle scheduling and scoped seeds.
nodes.details: Events may run at startup, reset, or intervals. The manager owns callable resolution, per-event scheduling, and reproducible invocation streams. Randomization is one family of event functors, alongside deterministic scene updates.
boundaries: Event functors follow the event-manager contract, not observation or reward signatures.

nodes.label: Rigid objects
nodes.summary: Represents rigid scene objects and their physical state.
nodes.details: SimulationManager creates and retains rigid entities. Their object facade exposes batched poses and physics properties through the selected backend.
boundaries: Supported operations depend on the object type and selected physics backend.

nodes.label: Articulations
nodes.summary: Represents jointed scene entities and articulated state.
nodes.details: Articulations own joint and link state interfaces. Robot extends this object family with control parts, robot presets, kinematics, and motion-facing capabilities.
boundaries: Supported operations depend on the object type and selected physics backend.

nodes.label: Deformable objects
nodes.summary: Represents Newton-backed deformable particle-set entities.
nodes.details: Surface and volume deformable facades adapt typed particle-set state for simulation and visualization. Their creation and lifecycle are owned by SimulationManager.
boundaries: Supported operations depend on the object type and selected physics backend.

nodes.label: Device controller
nodes.summary: Maps input-device state to robot joint commands with joint-limit handling.
nodes.details: The controller retains a robot and one or more input devices. It produces actions for a host loop to consume in Gym or simulation, while device implementations own acquisition of controller state.
boundaries: The host remains responsible for applying actions and advancing the environment.

nodes.label: Trajectory computation
nodes.summary: Shared interpolation, resampling, timing, and trajectory warping algorithms.
nodes.details: Motion generators, playback adapters, and augmentation operators share these numerical operations. Timing and geometric transformations remain separate from robot state, environment stepping, and durable data storage.
boundaries: Compute must not import simulation objects or environment managers.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Trajectory computations on arrays and tensors.

Interpolation retains keyframe boundaries; resampling treats interior points
as optional path samples. Warping applies keyframe offsets to a trajectory."""

nodes.label: Kinematics computation
nodes.summary: Shared numerical kinematics and manipulability algorithms.
nodes.details: This package owns reusable numerical routines and private Warp kernels. Stateful robot solving remains in motion.solvers, while workspace analysis consumes shared metrics and kinematic computation.
boundaries: Numerical kernels do not own live robot or environment state.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Kinematics computations and scalar motion profiles.

Private Warp kernels implement FEP, OPW, SRS, UR, and trapezoidal/Double-S profiles.
Stateful solver interfaces and robot configuration remain in
``embodichain.lab.sim.motion.solvers``.
Pure batched manipulability helpers live in :mod:`.manipulability`."""

nodes.label: DatasetManager
nodes.summary: Coordinates dataset functors for frame collection, saving, and finalization.
nodes.details: Environment lifecycle operations dispatch recording actions through this manager. Recorders own their persistence backends. Finalization drains committed work; the host must explicitly decide which episodes to save or discard.
boundaries: Finalization is not an implicit commit of a live rollout.

nodes.label: LeRobot recording
nodes.summary: Persists demonstrations and metadata in LeRobot datasets with optional depth sidecars.
nodes.details: The recorder buffers environment frames, commits selected episode fragments, and tracks finalization. Action features follow the expert-action schema. Optional depth video is stored alongside the main dataset with metadata linking the outputs.
boundaries: A sidecar failure after the LeRobot commit cannot roll back the committed episode.

nodes.label: Async recording
nodes.summary: Moves durable dataset writes to one background worker.
nodes.details: The recorder copies tensor payloads to CPU and snapshots metadata before enqueueing. A FIFO worker owns persistence; finalization drains the queue, joins the worker, and surfaces failures.
boundaries: The queue is unbounded; writer lag can grow memory use.

nodes.label: Depth sidecar writer
nodes.summary: Coordinates depth-video files and metadata alongside recorded demonstrations.
nodes.details: Depth sidecars preserve depth observations separately from the primary dataset. Writer and reader utilities own encoding, output paths, and metadata required to associate depth frames with recorded episodes.
boundaries: Depth output is a separate persistence boundary from the LeRobot episode commit.

nodes.label: OnlineDataset
nodes.summary: Exposes live engine samples as an infinite PyTorch IterableDataset.
nodes.details: The dataset samples trajectory chunks from a started OnlineDataEngine. It supports item and batch modes with fixed or sampled chunk sizes. Worker lifecycle and shared-memory ownership remain in the engine.
boundaries: Dataset iteration does not own engine startup or shutdown.

nodes.label: Training assembly
nodes.summary: Builds environments, policies, algorithms, and the compatible trainer from configuration.
nodes.details: Training selects either a registered simulator Gym deployment or a lightweight learning environment. Algorithm rollout semantics determine the trainer and collector path. Evaluation, checkpointing, and runtime options are assembled here.
boundaries: Differentiable training is supported through the lightweight learning-environment route.

nodes.label: RL algorithms
nodes.summary: Registers PPO, GRPO, and APG with their rollout contracts.
nodes.details: Standard algorithms consume collected rollout data. APG consumes graph-connected differentiable rollouts. The algorithm registry provides configuration and construction while trainers own collection and update scheduling.
boundaries: Standard and differentiable rollout payloads are not interchangeable.

nodes.label: Policy models
nodes.summary: Defines policy action inference and model interfaces.
nodes.details: Actor-critic and actor-only implementations build on policy contracts and registered model configurations. Differentiable training requires graph-preserving action sampling; standard rollout collection has its own inference requirements.
boundaries: Policy inference does not own environment or trainer lifecycles.

nodes.label: SyncCollector
nodes.summary: Collects standard vector-environment rollouts into the training buffer.
nodes.details: The collector connects policy inference to environment stepping and records transition fields needed by standard algorithms. Bootstrap and actor/critic observation contracts are shared with the rollout buffer.
boundaries: Standard collection is separate from differentiable rollout collection.

nodes.label: Rollout buffer
nodes.summary: Stores standard rollout transitions and bootstrap state in TensorDict buffers.
nodes.details: The buffer preallocates vectorized rollout storage for collection and later updates. It preserves the transition fields and observation groups expected by algorithms and collectors.
boundaries: Graph-connected APG rollouts do not pass through this standard buffer.

nodes.label: DifferentiableTrainer
nodes.summary: Coordinates graph-connected rollouts and analytic policy-gradient updates.
nodes.details: The trainer supports segmented and complete differentiable rollouts through the lightweight environment protocol. It controls gradient lifetime, optimizer updates, and evaluation without converting the rollout to the standard buffer.
boundaries: The public training route does not connect this trainer directly to DifferentiableEnv.

nodes.label: Differentiable collector
nodes.summary: Collects differentiable trajectories while preserving their autograd graph.
nodes.details: This collector produces graph-connected rollout segments for analytic policy gradients. Environment state detachment defines truncation boundaries; scheduled complete rollouts retain the required horizon.
boundaries: Detaching rollout rewards or actions breaks the gradient path.

nodes.label: Learning environments
nodes.summary: Defines lightweight vector-environment protocols and factory registration.
nodes.details: Registered lightweight environments can support standard or differentiable rollouts. Differentiable protocols add state-detachment and optional scheduled-rollout hooks. This route is selected separately from simulator Gym configurations.
boundaries: A lightweight environment protocol is distinct from the Gym DifferentiableEnv class.

evidence.excerpt: """Contracts and registration helpers for lightweight learning environments."""

nodes.label: Policy evaluation
nodes.summary: Runs trained policy evaluation in headless or viewer workflows.
nodes.details: The evaluation entry point resolves model inputs and environment configuration, then builds a compatible runtime or profile workflow. Reports and viewer integration expose the resulting evaluation artifacts.
boundaries: Evaluation consumes a trained policy; it is separate from training updates.

evidence.excerpt: """Unified policy evaluation for EmbodiChain training runs."""

nodes.label: SimReady pipeline
nodes.summary: Ingests raw assets through parsing and conversion stages into SimReady outputs.
nodes.details: The general asset-ingest pipeline coordinates parser capabilities and persisted processing state for supported input formats. Scene Engine also has an internal asset-preparation flow; these are distinct entry points.
boundaries: A converted asset is not a complete runnable Gym deployment.

nodes.label: Scene editing
nodes.summary: Edits an existing portable scene using a typed edit plan.
nodes.details: The editor imports scene state, interprets requested edits, prepares added assets, updates layout, and exports the result. It preserves the scene graph and object identity contracts needed for further editing.
boundaries: Editing operates on scene artifacts rather than a live Gym environment.

nodes.label: Scene export
nodes.summary: Writes portable scene metadata and assets for downstream simulation preparation.
nodes.details: The export boundary packages scene state, graph metadata, and referenced mesh or articulated assets. It owns coordinate and persistence conventions for portable output; runtime scene loading is a separate operation.
boundaries: A scene export still needs task and embodiment configuration to become a deployment.

nodes.label: GraspKit
nodes.summary: Defines parallel-jaw gripper models and grasp-pose generation interfaces.
nodes.details: Input: target meshes and explicit parallel-jaw gripper geometry. Output: candidate grasp poses or annotated contact pairs, depending on the operation. Entry: the public AntipodalGraspPoseGenerator API for generation, or embodichain annotate-grasp for interactive region annotation. Shared interfaces and gripper models are defined by graspkit.pose_generator.
boundaries: A geometric grasp candidate is not proof of successful physical grasping.

nodes.label: URDF assembly
nodes.summary: Assembles URDF components, connections, sensors, and mesh resources.
nodes.details: Input: registered URDF components, connection rules, sensor attachments, and mesh resources. Output: merged URDF XML, a saved URDF file, and copied mesh resources. Entry: construct URDFAssemblyManager, call add_component()/attach_sensor(), then merge_urdfs(output_path). This branch is a Python API, not a registered unified CLI command.
boundaries: Assembly prepares descriptions; it does not execute robot control.

nodes.label: Convex decomposition
nodes.summary: Prepares convex collision meshes for URDF assets.
nodes.details: Input: a URDF and its referenced meshes, with optional scale and inertia-recomputation settings. Output: convex collision meshes and an updated URDF. Entry: embodichain decompose-urdf --urdf_path <path>; the CLI delegates to generate_urdf_collision_convexes().
boundaries: Collision-mesh preparation does not validate an entire robot task.

nodes.label: Program loading & validation
nodes.summary: Loads bounded JSON or YAML into the canonical Task Program configuration.
nodes.details: Input loading, strict decoding, and reference validation establish a declarative program before compilation. Host-controlled integration choices and supported language constructs remain explicit at this boundary.
boundaries: Successful decoding is not successful execution or physical qualification.

evidence.excerpt: """Safe file and strict JSON loading for declarative Task Programs."""

nodes.label: SceneRegistry
nodes.summary: Binds semantic entity identifiers to scene metadata and runtime providers.
nodes.details: The registry supplies entity, affordance, geometry, and collision-world information to semantic analysis and execution. Static manifest construction and live provider access remain separate operations.
boundaries: Registry metadata alone does not establish a measured physical outcome.

nodes.label: RobotSkillProfile
nodes.summary: Declares robot resources, skill bindings, and effect-assurance capabilities.
nodes.details: Profiles connect semantic intent to available robot resources and Atomic Skills. Bound profiles resolve concrete endpoints and integration choices while preserving declared capability and assurance constraints.
boundaries: A declared capability does not replace runtime evidence or acceptance checks.

nodes.label: Integration catalog
nodes.summary: Describes one Task Program integration and validates compilation against its fingerprint.
nodes.details: A task registration owns this immutable provider-free directory of scene, robot-profile, runtime, and extension declarations. Preflight checks bind compilation to the integration fingerprint before live assembly uses that registration.
boundaries: The catalog describes a registration; it does not own physical Gym component composition.

nodes.label: Effect evidence
nodes.summary: Collects typed evidence from registered providers for semantic effects.
nodes.details: Evidence queries identify the observations required for an effect. Registered providers supply typed batches which monitors evaluate against declared expectations. Command dispatch and observed physical effects are separate facts.
boundaries: Missing or projected evidence must not be presented as measured success.

nodes.label: Parallel execution
nodes.summary: Coordinates parallel semantic branches through command and safety interfaces.
nodes.details: Parallel execution coordinates branch lifecycles, lane commands, shared timing, and safety validation. It depends on integration-supplied capabilities and resource contracts rather than assuming arbitrary commands are safe to combine.
boundaries: Parallel execution support is conditional on the selected integration and safety contracts.

nodes.label: Rigid object groups
nodes.summary: Groups multiple rigid bodies into a batched scene entity.
nodes.details: RigidObjectGroup maintains an environment-by-object layout with indexed state and physical properties in RigidBodyGroupData. SimulationManager declares and binds the group through Spawn; it is a separate BatchEntity facade, not a subclass of RigidObject.
boundaries: Grouped bodies are not an articulated joint hierarchy.

nodes.label: Lights
nodes.summary: Controls light color, intensity, falloff, and pose through a batched facade.
nodes.details: SimulationManager creates global lights or per-arena lights according to LightCfg. Light provides indexed rendering-property updates and reset behavior through BatchEntity.
boundaries: Global light types have one shared render light; other types are replicated per arena.

nodes.label: Gizmo
nodes.summary: Provides native robot IK and browser manipulation controls for simulation targets.
nodes.details: SimulationManager retains and updates Gizmo handles. A handle references a robot, rigid object, or camera; robot control uses a selected control part and IK solver. Native entity-root manipulation is managed separately through enable_entity_gizmo.
boundaries: Gizmo supports exactly one simulation environment and is not a BatchEntity subclass.

nodes.label: Rigid constraints
nodes.summary: Wraps per-arena fixed constraints between two rigid objects.
nodes.details: The manager creates native fixed constraints and stores their handles with references to both RigidObject endpoints. Inactive arenas retain empty handle slots, so indexing remains aligned with environment IDs.
boundaries: Currently a Default-backend resource; only fixed constraints are supported. This wrapper does not inherit BatchEntity.

nodes.label: Surface deformables
nodes.summary: Specializes deformable objects for cloth particle sets.
nodes.details: SurfaceDeformableObject extends DeformableObject with the surface topology discriminator. SimulationManager.add_deformable_object selects the facade from configuration; shared DeformableObjectData exposes particle positions and velocities. ClothObject is a compatibility alias for this class.
boundaries: Requires a supported Newton solver and CUDA device; Default and gradient-enabled deformable state mutation are unsupported.

nodes.label: Volume deformables
nodes.summary: Specializes deformable objects for volumetric soft-body particle sets.
nodes.details: VolumeDeformableObject extends the shared deformable facade and retains tetrahedral boundary triangles for collision-surface queries. Particle state uses DeformableObjectData; SoftObject is a compatibility alias for this class.
boundaries: Requires a supported Newton solver and CUDA device; render topology and tetrahedral collision-surface topology are distinct.

nodes.label: Object backend views
nodes.summary: Adapts rigid and articulated object state to backend-neutral Scene batches.
nodes.details: RigidBodyViewBase and ArticulationViewBase define the contracts; SceneRigidBodyView and SceneArticulationView normalize tensor layouts and indexed access. Supporting adapters handle drives, geometry, state, physical properties, controls, collision, and lifecycle.
boundaries: Object-state adapters do not select the physics solver or own SimulationManager stepping.

nodes.label: BatchEntity
nodes.summary: Defines shared configuration and instance operations for batched simulation entities.
nodes.details: RigidObject, RigidObjectGroup, Articulation, Light, and DeformableObject use this base; Robot inherits through Articulation. It carries common identity, configuration, device, and entity indexing. Gizmo and RigidConstraint have separate wrapper contracts.
boundaries: Inheritance describes a shared interface; it does not guarantee every object supports the same physical operations.

nodes.label: Chunk samplers
nodes.summary: Selects fixed-shape time windows using configurable chunk-length distributions.
nodes.details: ChunkSizeSampler defines the length-selection interface. UniformChunkSampler draws integer lengths from a closed interval; GMMChunkSampler draws from a Gaussian mixture. In batch mode, OnlineDataset draws one length per yield, shared across trajectories. Item mode fixes one length per iterator for consistent DataLoader collation.
boundaries: Length selection does not determine whether the engine has an eligible, unlocked continuous trajectory window.

nodes.label: Depth sidecar reader
nodes.summary: Loads depth metadata and decodes episode/sensor depth video frames.
nodes.details: DepthVideoLibrary indexes sidecars by episode and sensor. DepthVideoReader lazily decodes and caches one video, then dequantizes frames using its metadata. load_depth_dataset pairs a LeRobot dataset with its depth library.
boundaries: Reader access consumes persisted sidecars; it does not read the online engine shared-memory buffer.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Readers for compressed depth sidecar videos.

Decodes the ``gray12le``/HEVC MP4s written by :class:`DepthSidecarManager` and
dequantizes them back to metres or millimetres. ``load_depth_dataset`` composes
a LeRobot dataset with its depth sidecar library so callers can read RGB, state,
action, mask and depth together.
"""

nodes.label: Depth quantization
nodes.summary: Converts depth values to and from the sidecar video representation.
nodes.details: The writer quantizes depth maps into 12-bit integer codes; the reader dequantizes decoded frames using the recorded range and mapping. Logarithmic and linear modes share a metadata contract.
boundaries: Video codec losslessness does not eliminate quantization error in the original floating-point depth.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Depth quantization/dequantization for compressed depth sidecar videos.

Depth maps are packed into 12-bit integer codes (``uint16``, values
``0…DEPTH_QMAX``) so they fit the ``gray12le`` pixel format and can be encoded
losslessly by HEVC (``libx265``). Logarithmic quantization is the default
because it allocates more quanta to near-range depth, matching the
``1/depth`` error profile of typical depth sensors.

The math is ported from lerobot 0.6.0 (itself adapted from BEHAVIOR-1K's
``obs_utils.py``) and depends only on :mod:`av`, :mod:`numpy` and
:mod:`torch` -- all of which run on Python 3.10--3.12. See issue #424.
"""

nodes.label: Scene understanding
nodes.summary: Interprets an image, segments objects, and initializes a validated support graph.
nodes.details: The image-generation entry calls this stage with VLM and segmentation clients. It builds semantic objects, validates masks, and obtains a scene graph keyed by known object IDs.
boundaries: Model output and segmentation results are validated before downstream geometry generation.

nodes.label: Asset generation & refinement
nodes.summary: Generates geometry and articulated assets, then refines scene placement.
nodes.details: This stage generates coarse geometry from masks, optionally generates articulated USDC assets, runs the Scene Engine SimReady processor, and refines object placement using the validated support graph.
boundaries: External geometry and articulation services are configured clients; scene generation does not register a runnable Gym deployment.

nodes.label: Scene asset preparation
nodes.summary: Prepares generated Scene Engine geometry for layout and export.
nodes.details: The Scene Engine processor consumes coarse assets and layout metadata, then prepares the geometry used during placement refinement and export. Its configuration controls scale and pose processing within scene generation.
boundaries: This internal Scene Engine processor is separate from the general single-asset SimReady ingestion pipeline.

nodes.label: Scene edit layout
nodes.summary: Reconstructs scene placement against an edited goal graph.
nodes.details: The edit pipeline identifies add/move variables and delegates graph-constrained placement to SceneLayoutConstructor. The previous scene, added assets, and updated graph define the inputs; the resulting scene is exported by the caller.
boundaries: This entry owns the edit-layout stage; image-generation refinement is a separate entry.

nodes.label: Scene import
nodes.summary: Reconstructs an editable scene and graph from a portable scene export.
nodes.details: The importer validates scene_export metadata and object/graph identity, reconstructs assets and editable scene state, and supplies the edit pipeline. Import/export form the portable scene boundary.
boundaries: Editable scene coordinates and portable runtime coordinates differ; body scale remains separate from mesh geometry.

nodes.label: Asset parser stages
nodes.summary: Dispatches inspector, geometry, physics, USD, and internal asset parsers.
nodes.details: ParserManager registers the supported parser implementations and runs the selected stage names for an ingested asset. Individual parsers own their metadata and resume behavior; the manager records parsed status after the pipeline completes.
boundaries: Pipeline stages belong to single-asset ingestion, not the Scene Engine geometry processor.

nodes.label: GenSim UI sessions
nodes.summary: Tracks one replaceable subprocess per Gradio session.
nodes.details: SessionProcessRegistry coordinates session-owned subprocess replacement, cancellation, and cleanup for the GenSim web interface. Command construction and environment handling live alongside this registry.
boundaries: This is web-session process ownership, not an in-process call edge to every generation stage.

nodes.label: PPO
nodes.summary: Optimizes an actor-critic policy from standard TensorDict rollouts.
nodes.details: PPO computes generalized advantage estimates and a clipped policy objective with configurable value loss over shuffled rollout minibatches. Collection and bootstrap storage belong to SyncCollector and RolloutBuffer.
boundaries: Uses standard rollouts; it does not backpropagate through environment dynamics.

nodes.label: GRPO
nodes.summary: Optimizes policies with group-relative advantages from standard rollouts.
nodes.details: GRPO uses grouped environments and relative-return advantages while consuming the standard collection/storage path. Actor-only policies can provide its action-distribution interface without a learned value function.
boundaries: The configured environment count must satisfy the algorithm grouping contract.

nodes.label: APG
nodes.summary: Optimizes policy parameters through differentiable rollout rewards.
nodes.details: APG supports segmented and complete-rollout gradient accumulation before optimizer updates. DifferentiableTrainer and DifferentiableCollector retain the required computation graph.
boundaries: Requires differentiable learning environments and graph-preserving actions; the simulator Gym training route rejects this algorithm.

nodes.label: ActorCritic
nodes.summary: Provides Gaussian actions and value estimates with separate actor and critic inputs.
nodes.details: The policy composes actor and critic networks, action-distribution parameters, and optional per-stream empirical observation normalization. Ordered observation groups can differ between actor and critic.
boundaries: This model owns policy inference; the algorithm and trainer own optimization and rollout execution.

nodes.label: ActorOnly
nodes.summary: Provides Gaussian actions without a learned value network.
nodes.details: ActorOnly implements the Policy interface with zero value outputs and supports reparameterized action sampling for differentiable consumers. The actor network and trainable distribution scale define its action distribution.
boundaries: The absence of a critic does not select the trainer; rollout kind is selected by the algorithm.

nodes.label: Running observation normalization
nodes.summary: Normalizes continuous observation fields with explicit running-statistic updates.
nodes.details: Running Welford statistics support a mask that preserves semantic fields. DifferentiableTrainer optionally creates or accepts this normalizer; normalize itself does not update statistics, allowing a fixed transform during complete rollouts.
boundaries: This differentiable-training helper is distinct from ActorCritic per-stream empirical normalizers.

nodes.label: Parallel-jaw gripper model
nodes.summary: Defines physical gripper dimensions independently of the sampling algorithm.
nodes.details: Input: opening limits, finger dimensions, palm depth, and a model identifier. Output: validated geometry configuration shared by compatible parallel-jaw generators. Entry: ParallelJawGripperModelCfg or get_parallel_jaw_gripper_model().
boundaries: A gripper geometry description is not a robot controller.

nodes.label: Antipodal grasp generator
nodes.summary: Generates candidate grasp poses through a reusable parallel-jaw interface.
nodes.details: Input: target mesh vertices/triangles, gripper geometry, sampling and collision policies. Output: valid or ranked grasp poses; prepare_mesh() also exposes annotated antipodal pairs. Entry: AntipodalGraspPoseGenerator.prepare_mesh(), get_valid_grasp_poses(), or get_best_grasp_poses().
boundaries: Geometric candidates do not prove reachability or physical grasp success.

nodes.label: Mesh grasp backend
nodes.summary: Coordinates sampling, annotation, collision checks, and caches for one mesh.
nodes.details: Input: one target-local mesh and resolved generation/collision settings. Output: cached antipodal pairs and mesh-specific grasp candidates. Entry: created lazily by AntipodalGraspPoseGenerator._backend().
boundaries: Private implementation detail; applications should use the public generator API.

nodes.label: Antipodal sampling
nodes.summary: Samples opposing surface contacts using mesh ray casting.
nodes.details: Input: a triangle mesh and sampling/deviation parameters. Output: antipodal point pairs used to construct grasp candidates. Entry: AntipodalSampler, normally created by the mesh backend.
boundaries: Contact-pair sampling alone does not check the complete gripper collision geometry.

nodes.label: Gripper collision checks
nodes.summary: Checks gripper geometry against the target mesh.
nodes.details: Input: object mesh, gripper dimensions, and candidate grasp transforms. Output: collision results used to filter grasp candidates. Entry: GripperCollisionChecker through the mesh backend.
boundaries: Target-mesh collision checking is not full-scene motion planning.

nodes.label: Interactive grasp annotation
nodes.summary: Offers browser selection of a graspable mesh region.
nodes.details: Input: a mesh path and CLI sampling, gripper-width, and viewer settings. Output: selected-region antipodal pairs and backend annotation cache data. Entry: embodichain annotate-grasp; invokes the public generator with interactive annotation enabled.
boundaries: Annotation prepares geometry; it does not execute a grasp.

nodes.label: URDF components
nodes.summary: Processes component links, joints, naming, and mesh references.
nodes.details: Input: registered component descriptions and a shared mesh manager. Output: processed component elements with consistent names and rewritten mesh references. Entry: URDFAssemblyManager.add_component() registers inputs; merge_urdfs() delegates component processing.
boundaries: Components describe robot structure; they are not live simulation entities.

nodes.label: URDF connections
nodes.summary: Applies component connection rules and sensor attachment joints.
nodes.details: Input: processed links/joints, a base link, connection rules, and attachment transforms. Output: connection joints forming the assembled robot description. Entry: URDFConnectionManager inside URDFAssemblyManager.merge_urdfs().
boundaries: Connection rules encode assembly structure, not runtime motion constraints.

nodes.label: URDF sensor attachments
nodes.summary: Processes sensor descriptions and attachment metadata for assembly.
nodes.details: Input: sensor sources, names, types, parent links, and transforms. Output: processed sensor elements and attachment data for URDF assembly. Entry: URDFAssemblyManager.attach_sensor() and the sensor manager used during merge.
boundaries: Sensor description assembly does not start a device driver or simulated sensor stream.

nodes.label: URDF mesh resources
nodes.summary: Copies mesh resources and rewrites references for the assembled robot.
nodes.details: Input: source mesh files, output directory, and component/sensor naming. Output: copied mesh resources and updated mesh references. Entry: URDFMeshManager shared by component and sensor managers.
boundaries: Resource copying is separate from convex collision decomposition.

nodes.label: URDF file output
nodes.summary: Formats and persists the assembled URDF document.
nodes.details: Input: merged XML elements, output path, and optional module metadata. Output: a formatted URDF file with assembly sections. Entry: URDFFileWriter.write_urdf(), called by merge_urdfs().
boundaries: Writing a URDF does not validate a complete simulation task.

nodes.label: URDF collision processor
nodes.summary: Replaces mesh collisions with convex pieces and optionally recomputes inertia.
nodes.details: Input: a URDF, referenced meshes, hull-count limit, and optional scale/inertia flags. Output: convex collision mesh files and a rewritten URDF. Entry: generate_urdf_collision_convexes() orchestrates URDFModifider.decompose_collisions() and save_urdf().
boundaries: Inertia recomputation and scaling are optional; non-mesh geometries are not decomposed.
